title: Eshnunna of the Eternal Flame
dek: The inner citadel reached beyond Ciaránach’s streets, with a distinct threshold within the pilgrimage.

body:
Eshnunna is the inner sanctuary encountered during the pilgrimage into Ciaránach. The narrator identifies the citadel after a further climb through the city’s quiet streets, then describes another threshold: the holy of holies, Eshnunna of the Eternal Flame.

An inner place, not a second capital

The journey begins at Zarathis, ascends the holy road and enters Ciaránach before reaching Eshnunna. The named sanctuary therefore has its own identity within the holy city. It is not the whole of Ciaránach, a new name for Zarathis, or a separately mapped settlement.

Earlier regional references also associate the holy place with Seraphis. That association does not relocate the pilgrimage’s explicitly narrated approach or establish that Seraphis and Ciaránach are interchangeable. A full plan of the sacred geography remains unavailable.

The threshold and its limits

Access is part of the pilgrimage’s permission-bound encounter with sacred knowledge. Reaching a named sanctuary is distinct from having unrestricted access to everything its custodians preserve. The Golden Ones’ claims and visitors’ interpretations do not become universal truth merely because they are spoken here.

The public location record preserves the name, approach and relationship to Ciaránach. The inner revelations remain protected. The Eternal Flame’s exact nature, a complete floor plan, routine access arrangements and the sanctuary’s full custodial history are not supplied by its name or artwork.
